html:
Discounts are where CPQ earns (and loses) its money. Every implementation lives or dies on the gap between list price and net price — the discount — and the rules that decide who gets which discount under which conditions. This module, Phase 05 of the Academy, teaches the price book spine, the Discount_Schedule__c volume tiers, the price-rule engine that resolves those tiers, and the quote-level math that turns per-line net prices into Total_ARR__c and Discount_Percent__c.

Everything here is driven by two Apex services: PriceRuleEngineService (which tier applies to which line) and QuoteCalculatorService (which totals land on the quote). Both are bulk-safe, share-aware, and boundary-guarded — exactly the shape your production pricing code should have.

Learning objectives

  • Trace the price book spine: list price from PricebookEntry.UnitPrice, defended against nulls by List_Unit_Price__c.
  • Distinguish list price, net price, per-line discount %, and quote-level discount %.
  • Model volume tiers on Discount_Schedule__c and know which fields bound a tier.
  • Explain why the highest matching tier wins and how a blank Product_Family__c acts as a global fallback.
  • Resolve a single line's discount with PriceRuleEngineService.resolveDiscountPercent.
  • Batch-apply price rules to hundreds of lines with applyPriceRules using exactly two SOQL statements.
  • Recompute quote totals and discount leakage with QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals.
  • Understand block pricing and tiered pricing as the two real-world discount structures.
  • Compute renewal ARR with uplift (ARR × (1 + Uplift_Percent__c/100)).
  • Identify the pricing facts tested by the CPQ Specialist (Pricing 16%) and Revenue Cloud Consultant (CPQ 18%) blueprints.

List price, net price, and the discount gap

Every price conversation starts with three numbers per line:

TermFieldMeaning
List priceList_Unit_Price__c (falls back to UnitPrice)The published standard price
Net priceNet_Unit_Price__c (falls back to UnitPrice)What the customer actually pays
Discount %(list − net) / list × 100The concession, per line

The quote-level numbers are the same idea aggregated:

text
listTotal = Σ quantity × List_Unit_Price__c
netTotal  = Σ quantity × Net_Unit_Price__c
discount% = (listTotal − netTotal) / listTotal × 100

QuoteCalculatorService implements precisely this. Two details matter:

  • Null safety: the engine treats a missing Net_Unit_Price__c as "no discount" (net = list), so a quote can never divide by zero.
  • Rounding: all money is setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP), the accounting standard.
soql
SELECT Id, List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Quantity,
       (List_Unit_Price__c - Net_Unit_Price__c) / List_Unit_Price__c * 100 line_discount_pct
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE Quote.Total_ARR__c > 0
Tip — "Discount leakage" is exactly discount% aggregated to deal level. When sales reports "we always give 20%," report leakage back at them: Opportunity.Discount_Leakage_Percent__c is the deal-level metric the whole pricing engine defends.

Discount schedules: the volume tier table

The Academy prices volume with Discount_Schedule__c. A tier row looks like this:

text
Discount_Type__c   = 'Volume'
Lower_Bound__c     = 5000        (inclusive)
Upper_Bound__c     = 9999        (inclusive)   — null means "open-ended"
Discount_Percent__c = 10
Product_Family__c  = 'Software'  (blank = global fallback)
Active__c          = true
json
{
  "name": "Volume tier 10%",
  "type": "Volume",
  "range": [5000, 9999],
  "discountPercent": 10,
  "family": "Software",
  "active": true
}

Tiers are inclusive: a row matches when Lower_Bound__c <= amount AND (Upper_Bound__c IS NULL OR Upper_Bound__c >= amount). When several tiers match, the highest discount wins — never the first row entered.

SeriesSoftware $/moEligible discount
10 – 1,0005%
21,001 – 5,0008%
35,001 – 20,00012%
420,001+15%

A $6,000 software purchase matches only tier 3 → 12%, not 15% (outside its cap) and not 8% (lower wins). A $25,000 support purchase gets 0% unless a support-family schedule exists — family matching is exact.

The price-rule engine: matching tiers

PriceRuleEngineService has two entry points sharing one in-memory resolver:

apex
// Single-rule lookup (UI helpers, admin tools)
public static Decimal resolveDiscountPercent(String productFamily, Decimal amount)

It runs one SOQL: active, Volume schedules whose bounds contain the amount. The family filter executes in the resolver with exact string equality, and a blank family is a wildcard. Then the batch path:

apex
// Batch path (trigger-time, bulk-safe): returns line.Id -> discount %
public static Map<Id, Decimal> applyPriceRules(List<QuoteLineItem> lines)

The batch path is deliberately two SOQL queries total:

  1. One query joins PricebookEntry → Product2.Family for every line's entry id (resolves each line's family).
  2. One query loads all active volume rules.
  3. Resolution happens in memory — per-line, zero extra governor budget.
InputReturn
1 line, Family Software, list 6,000{ lineId: 12.00 }
200 lines, mixed familiesMap of 200 entries, resolved against preloaded rules
null / empty listEmpty map (boundary guard, never throws)
Line with no matching family0.00 (no rule applicable)
apex
Map<Id, Decimal> discounts = PriceRuleEngineService.applyPriceRules(lines);
for (QuoteLineItem li : lines) {
    li.Discount_Percent__c = discounts.get(li.Id);
}

Block pricing and tiered pricing

Real discount logic comes in two canonical shapes, and the exam tests both:

ShapeHow it pricesExample
Block pricingEvery unit in a block gets the block's rate; different blocks can price differentlyFirst 100 seats at 20, next 100 at 15
Tiered pricingThe entire quantity gets the rate of the tier it falls into (best tier wins)150 seats → everything at the "101–200" tier

resolveDiscountPercent implements tiered behavior against a dollar amount — the classic volume-discount semantics. Block pricing would instead iterate per-block and sum the pieces. The two are frequently mistaken for each other in requirements documents, so the consultant's first question is always: does the 101st unit change the price of units 1–100?

  • If yes → tiered (all-at-tier).
  • If no → block (each slice keeps its own rate).

Quote-level math and the trigger path

Pricing doesn't stop at the line. QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(Set<Id> quoteIds) re-aggregates every line of every given quote in one SOQL + one DML:

apex
public static void recalculateTotals(Set<Id> quoteIds) {
    if (quoteIds == null || quoteIds.isEmpty()) { return; }   // boundary guard
    Map<Id, QuoteSummary> summaries = new Map<Id, QuoteSummary>();
    List<QuoteLineItem> lines = [ /* SELECT all lines WHERE QuoteId IN :quoteIds */ ];
    // aggregate list/net in memory, then:
    //   quote.Total_ARR__c       = netTotal
    //   quote.Discount_Percent__c = calculateDiscountPercent(list, net)
    // update quotesToUpdate;    // one DML for the whole batch
}

A production trigger wires this to the line object so any line change re-prices instantly. The trigger handler pattern from Phase 01 guarantees thin triggers, unit-testable services, and a recursion guard so the recalculation updating the quote cannot re-fire the same work.

Worked golden-path numbers (the test asserts exactly these):

LineQtyList unitNet unitLine subtotal
Core41,000800list 4,000 / net 3,200
Quote totalARR 3,200, discount 20.00%

QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(new Set<Id>{ q.Id });
Quote check = [SELECT Total_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c FROM Quote WHERE Id = :q.Id];
System.debug(check.Total_ARR__c);        // 3200

Renewal pricing: ARR and uplift

Renewals reprice the deal at renewal time. The Academy's renewal pipeline computes the new value from the contract's ARR plus an uplift percent — the modern-of-quote-with-lift pattern the managed package does with SBQQ__Renewal__c records and renewal quotes.

text
renewalARR = contract.ARR__c × (1 + Uplift_Percent__c / 100)
3200 ARR, uplift 10%  ->  3200 × 1.10 = 3,520
apex
Decimal uplifted = contract.ARR__c * (1 + contract.Uplift_Percent__c / 100);

The golden-path test proves it end to end: 200 expiring contracts with 5% uplift produce 200 Renewal_Opportunity__c rows, the largest at 1050.00 (1000 × 1.05). Note that Renewal_Opportunity__c.ARR__c already includes uplift — never add it twice.

Pricing facts on the blueprints

Keep the exam weights honest when budgeting study time:

CertificationPricing weight on blueprint
CPQ SpecialistPricing 16% (third-largest domain)
Revenue Cloud ConsultantConfigure Price Quote (CPQ) 18%

Between the two, expect pricing scenario questions on: list vs net, discount math, tiered vs block semantics, sum of options in bundles, and renewal uplift. All of these are exactly the calculations you practiced in this module — arithmetic, not memorization.

Common pitfalls

  • First-row-wins mental model. Rules resolve highest tier wins, ordered by discount, not insertion order. Sort assumptions break the moment a schedule has overlapping tiers.
  • Family string mismatch. 'software' vs 'Software' never matches; family matching is exact. Standardize the family picklist and the Product_Family__c values.
  • Null net price treated as a genuine $0. The service falls back to UnitPrice, meaning "no net price" equals "list price," not a free product. Write the fallback explicitly yourself.
  • Apply rules per line in a loop. applyPriceRules loads rules once for 200 lines; calling resolveDiscountPercent per line would fire 200 SOQL queries and fail the 100-query limit.
  • Confusing block with tiered. The 101st unit changing units 1–100 means tiered; each slice keeping its own rate means block. Ask the requirement question before building.
  • Rolling up discounts twice. Discount_Percent__c on the quote is derived from totals; setting it manually on insert fights the calculator. Let recalculateTotals own it.
  • Forgetting the active flag. Inactive schedules silently stop pricing — and the failure mode is a 0% discount, which usually surfaces only at contract revenue time.

Key takeaways

  • List → net → discount: the whole pricing engine is (list − net) / list, at line level and deal level.
  • Discount_Schedule__c holds inclusive volume tiers; the highest matching tier wins, and a blank family is a global fallback.
  • PriceRuleEngineService resolves one rule or thousands with the same in-memory logic and exactly two SOQL statements on the batch path.
  • QuoteCalculatorService owns quote totals and discount leakage, guarded against nulls and rounded HALF_UP.
  • Block pricing and tiered pricing are different semantics — confirm the requirement before you build.
  • Renewal pricing compounds uplift once: ARR × (1 + uplift%), already baked into Renewal_Opportunity__c.ARR__c.
  • With catalog, configuration, data model, and pricing behind you, Phase 06 takes the priced configuration and turns it into the quote document the customer actually signs.
